s: Azariah, a prophet and son of Oded, is inspired by the Spirit of God to meet Asa, Judah and Benjamin, telling them the LORD stays with seekers, forsakes the forsaking, and urging strength for rewarded work.

l: Maacah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Maacah, King Asa's mother and queen mother, made an abominable image for an Asherah; Asa removed her from that position, then cut down, ground up, and burned the image at Kidron.

l: covenant to seek the LORD, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: A covenant made by the Jerusalem assembly in Asa's fifteenth year, third month, pledging to seek the LORD with all heart and soul, with death decreed for anyone who refused. The people swore loudly with trumpets and shouting, and afterward the LORD was found and gave rest.

l: Baasha, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Baasha is a king of Israel who built Ramah to blockade Asa's Judah, but abandoned the project and let the work cease when Ben Hadad's armies struck Israelite cities.

l: Ben Hadad, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Ben Hadad, king of Syria living at Damascus, son of an earlier king, accepted Asa's silver and gold and attacked Israel's northern cities; Hanani later rebuked Asa for relying on him.

l: Hanani, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: is_a seer Hanani the seer told Asa that relying on the king of Syria rather than the LORD was foolish, recalled the defeat of the Ethiopians and Lubim through reliance on the LORD, and warned Asa of wars to come. Asa was angry and put him in prison.

l: Ramah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Ramah was built by Baasha to block access to Asa's Judah. Building stopped when Ben Hadad attacked Israel's cities, and Asa and Judah carried away its stones and timber to build Geba and Mizpah.

l: treaty between Asa and Ben Hadad, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Asa proposed a treaty with Ben Hadad like the one between their fathers, sending silver and gold and asking him to break his treaty with Baasha. Ben Hadad agreed and attacked Israelite cities, which made Baasha withdraw from Ramah, though Hanani condemned Asa's reliance on Syria.

l: Jehoshaphat, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoshaphat is a king of Judah, son of Asa and Azubah, who became king at thirty-five and reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem (the text also once calls him king of Israel). He followed his father Asa's example and walked in the first ways of David. He sought the LORD, rejected the Baals, and removed the Asherah poles and high places, though the high places are later said to have remained. His reign begins with strengthening Judah against Israel: he garrisoned the fortified cities and the Ephraim cities Asa had taken, built fortresses and store cities, and kept a large army of mighty men in Jerusalem. He sent princes to teach in Judah's cities and gained great riches and honor. His alliance with Ahab led him to join the war on Ramoth Gilead. He insisted on inquiring of a true prophet of the LORD, was mistaken for Ahab in battle, cried out, and was saved when the LORD helped him. Returning to Jerusalem, he was rebuked by Jehu for helping the wicked, yet Jehu noted he had removed the Asheroth and set his heart to seek God. He then brought the people back to the LORD from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and appointed judges in the fortified cities, charging them to act in the fear of the LORD, with Levites, priests and family heads serving in Jerusalem. When a vast multitude came against him he proclaimed a fast, prayed, urged the people to trust the LORD, and sent singers before the army. Victory brought joy and rest on all sides. Later he allied with Ahaziah in a ship venture to Tarshish, condemned as wicked; the LORD wrecked the ships after Eliezer's rebuke. His acts are recorded in the history of Jehu son of Hanani. He died and was buried in David's city. His son Jehoram, the firstborn, received the kingdom, while his other sons received gifts and fortified cities. Elijah's letter later cites his ways as a standard Jehoram failed to meet.

l: princes (Jehoshaphat's princes), The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoshaphat's five princes (Ben Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, Micaiah) are sent in his third year to teach in Judah's cities, accompanied by Levites and priests.

l: Zechariah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada the priest, was a prophet and ruler of God's house, descended from the Kohathites and Asaph's line. Moved by God's Spirit, he warned the people that forsaking the LORD meant being forsaken. They conspired and stoned him at the king's command; he asked the LORD to repay.

l: priests, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: has_role sprinkling the blood [received from the Levites] The priests had not sanctified themselves in sufficient number at the usual time, and in the second month they were ashamed and sanctified themselves and brought burnt offerings into the LORD's house. They stood in their order, sprinkled the blood received from the Levites, praised the LORD, and finally blessed the people, with their prayer coming up to heaven.

l: teaching mission, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: A teaching mission commissioned by Jehoshaphat in the third year of his reign: princes, Levites, and priests Elishama and Jehoram carry the book of the LORD's law and travel through all Judah's cities, teaching the people.

l: Arabians, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Arabians, neighbors of the Ethiopians, bring Jehoshaphat flocks of rams and goats, later are stirred by the LORD against Jehoram, joining Philistines to invade Judah and plunder the king's family.

l: army of mighty men of valor, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Mighty men of valor stationed in Jerusalem serving King Jehoshaphat, organized by fathers' houses under captains: Judah's Adnah, Jehohanan, Amasiah, and Benjamin's Eliada and Jehozabad, commanding hundreds of thousands, besides troops in fortified cities.

l: Ahab, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Ahab is a king of Israel who persuades Jehoshaphat to join him at Ramoth Gilead, trusts his four hundred prophets, and imprisons Micaiah for prophesying evil. Disguised in battle, he is struck by a stray arrow and dies at sunset.

l: Zedekiah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Zedekiah appears under two figures in the records: son of Chenaanah, who made iron horns and falsely prophesied Ahab's victory over the Syrians, struck Micaiah, and was told he would hide in an inner room; and a king installed by Nebuchadnezzar in place of Jehoiachin at age twenty-one. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, did evil, stayed stiff-necked, refused to humble himself before Jeremiah, and rebelled despite his oath.

l: Joash, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Joash was a king's son of David's line, the son of Ahaziah of Judah. As an infant he was rescued by Jehoshabeath from the slaughter of the king's sons and hidden with his nurse for six years in God's house while Athaliah reigned. Jehoiada and his sons then crowned, covenanted, and anointed him amid rejoicing, guarded by Levites, and set him on the throne. He became king at seven and reigned forty years in Jerusalem; his mother was Zibiah of Beersheba. He did right in the LORD's eyes all the days of Jehoiada, who chose his two wives, and he commissioned temple repair. After Jehoiada died he heeded the princes, forsook the LORD, and ordered Zechariah stoned. The Syrians wounded him, and his servants killed him on his bed for the blood of Jehoiada's sons. He was buried in David's city, not the kings' tombs, and his son Amaziah succeeded him.

l: Ramoth Gilead, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: is_target_of battle at Ramoth Gilead [Ahab and Jehoshaphat go up to fight there] Ramoth Gilead is the place Ahab and Jehoshaphat decide to go to in battle against the Syrians, after Ahab's prophets promise God will deliver it into the king's hand. It is where Micaiah says Ahab will fall, and where Ahab is fatally wounded.

l: Syrians, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: The Syrian army, though only a small company, attacked Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed the people's princes, sent plunder to Damascus's king, and left Joash seriously wounded, victorious because Judah had forsaken the LORD.

l: captains of the chariots (king of Syria's), The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Chariot captains serving the king of Syria, ordered to fight only the king of Israel; they mistook Jehoshaphat for Ahab and attacked him, then turned back upon realizing he was not Israel's king.

l: prophets (Ahab's four hundred), The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Four hundred prophets gathered at Samaria's gate unanimously prophesied that Ahab should attack Ramoth Gilead and prosper. Micaiah said the LORD had put a lying spirit in their mouths, and the outcome proved their word false.

l: lying spirit, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: is_a spirit from the army of heaven [sent to entice Ahab] A spirit came out and stood before the LORD, volunteering to entice Ahab by being a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. The LORD told it that it would entice him and prevail, and to go and do so, according to Micaiah's account.

l: battle at Ramoth Gilead, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: has_outcome Ahab died [at about sunset] Ahab and Jehoshaphat went up to the battle, with Ahab disguised and Jehoshaphat in his robes. The Syrian chariot captains went after Jehoshaphat by mistake until he was delivered, and a random arrow wounded Ahab. The battle increased that day, and Ahab died at about sunset.

l: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehu, seer and son of Hanani, confronts King Jehoshaphat, rebuking him for helping the wicked and loving God's haters, warning of the LORD's wrath, yet acknowledging his removal of the Asheroth and seeking God.

l: judges (Jehoshaphat's judges in the fortified cities of Judah), The Second Book of Chronicles
s: judge_for LORD [not for man] Jehoshaphat set these judges in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city. He told them to consider what they do, since they judge not for man but for the LORD, who is with them in judgment, and to let the fear of the LORD be on them, with no iniquity, partiality, or bribes.

l: people of Judah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoshaphat went out among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers. Their controversies, between blood and blood, law and commandment, statutes and ordinances, were to be brought to the appointed judges in Jerusalem, who were to warn them against guilt toward the LORD.

l: judgment and justice, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Judgment is presented as being done for the LORD, in his fear, faithfully and with a perfect heart, free of iniquity, respect of persons, and bribes. Those judging controversies must warn people not to be guilty toward the LORD so that wrath does not come on them and their brothers, and are told to deal courageously, with Amariah the chief priest over the LORD's matters and Levites serving as officers.

l: Moab, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: was_spared_by Israel [during the exodus from Egypt] The children of Moab, with Ammon and some Meunites, come against Jehoshaphat to battle. Jehoshaphat notes that Israel had spared them when leaving Egypt. Moab and Ammon rise against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to destroy them, then help destroy one another.

l: Ammon, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: was_spared_by Israel [during the exodus from Egypt] The children of Ammon join Moab in coming against Judah, and Jehoshaphat laments that they repay Israel's earlier mercy. Ammon and Moab attack and destroy Mount Seir's inhabitants, then turn on each other until none escape.

l: Mount Seir, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: was_spared_by Israel [during the exodus from Egypt] The inhabitants of Mount Seir are named among those who came against Judah. The LORD's ambushers strike them, and Ammon and Moab rise up to kill and destroy them utterly.

l: Jahaziel, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jahaziel, a Levite of Asaph's sons and Zechariah's son, is seized by the LORD's Spirit amid the assembly and tells Judah not to fear, to go down tomorrow, and that they need not fight.

l: the LORD's house, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: The LORD's house is a holy site restricted to priests and ministering Levites, guarded by gatekeepers against the unclean. It hosted the covenant with the king, his coronation, Athaliah's removal before her death, and the storage of David's weapons. Athaliah's sons later broke it up and gave its dedicated things to the Baals. Joash restored and strengthened it, and offerings continued during Jehoiada's life, but the princes and people abandoned it, and Zechariah was stoned in its court.

l: Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Ahaziah, youngest son of Jehoram and Athaliah, became king of Judah at forty-two and reigned one year in Jerusalem. Guided by his mother and the house of Ahab, he did evil in the LORD's sight. He joined Jehoram of Israel against Hazael and visited the wounded Jehoram in Jezreel. Caught hiding in Samaria, he was killed by Jehu and buried as Jehoshaphat's son.

l: invasion of Judah by Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: ends_with mutual destruction of the invaders [LORD set ambushers; Judah did not fight] A great multitude of Moab, Ammon, and Meunites is reported at Hazazon Tamar (En Gedi), prompting Judah's fast and prayer. The invaders are destroyed without Judah fighting, as the LORD sets ambushers and the enemy forces turn on each other. Judah finds only dead bodies and spends three days taking plunder.

l: praise and singing, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: The Levites of the Kohathites and Korahites praise the LORD with an exceedingly loud voice, and Jehoshaphat appoints singers in holy array to go before the army saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for his loving kindness endures forever." When they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushers against the enemy. Judah later returns to Jerusalem with stringed instruments, harps, and trumpets.

l: Jehoram, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoram was Jehoshaphat's firstborn son, who received the kingdom and reigned eight years in Jerusalem as king of Judah, beginning at thirty-two. After strengthening himself he killed his brothers, married Ahab's daughter, followed the evil ways of Israel's kings, built high places, and led Judah astray. Having forsaken the LORD, he lost Libnah, saw his sons taken except Jehoahaz, and was struck with illness. He died unregretted and was buried in David's city, not the kings' tombs.

l: Jehoshaphat's sons (Jehoram's brothers), The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Six named sons of Jehoshaphat, Jehoram's brothers, received silver, gold, precious things and fortified Judah cities from their father, then were all killed by Jehoram, whom Elijah's letter says they surpassed.

l: Azariah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Azariah is a chief priest of the house of Zadok, also called ruler of God's house. In Chapter 26 he leads eighty priests in resisting King Uzziah's incense offering and expelling the leprous king. In Chapter 31 he answers Hezekiah about the heaps, credits the LORD's blessing, and helps appoint overseers.

l: Elijah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: is_a prophet Elijah the prophet sent Jehoram a letter delivering the LORD's word of judgment. It condemned him for not following Jehoshaphat and Asa, for following the kings of Israel, and for killing his brothers.

l: letter (Elijah's letter), The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Elijah's letter to Jehoram, in the LORD's name, condemns him for following Israel's kings, leading Judah astray, and killing his better brothers, then foretells a plague on his people and family and a bowel disease.

l: Jehoram's illness, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoram's incurable bowel disease, sent by the LORD after the invasion as Elijah's letter foretold, lasted two years until his bowels fell out and he died, unmourned and without a burning.

l: Athaliah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Athaliah, daughter of Omri, was mother and wicked counselor of Ahaziah. After her son died, she destroyed all the royal offspring of Judah's house and reigned over the land six years. When she heard the people praising the king, she entered the LORD's house, tore her clothes, and cried 'Treason!' Jehoiada had her removed and killed at the horse gate.

l: house of Ahab, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Ahab's house served as counselors to Ahaziah after his father's death, leading him to evil and to his destruction. Jehu, anointed by the LORD, was executing judgment on it and cutting it off.

l: Jehu the son of Nimshi, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehu, son of Nimshi, was anointed by the LORD to cut off Ahab's house; carrying out that judgment, he killed Judah's princes and Ahaziah's brothers' sons, and Ahaziah was brought to him and killed.

l: Jehoshabeath, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoshabeath is King Jehoram's daughter, Ahaziah's sister, and wife of Jehoiada the priest. She secretly rescued Joash from the slain king's sons, hiding him with his nurse so Athaliah could not kill him.

l: Jehoiada, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Jehoiada was a chief priest who, in the seventh year, covenanted with the captains and Levites, had the king's son crowned and anointed, had Athaliah killed, and ended Baal worship, restoring the temple's offerings and gatekeepers. He then guided King Joash, chose his two wives, and oversaw temple repair funds. He died at 130 and was buried among the kings in David's city for his good toward Israel and God. Afterward Joash killed his son Zechariah, and Joash's servants killed Joash.

l: royal offspring of the house of Judah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Athaliah destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah after her son Ahaziah died. Joash alone was rescued from among the king's sons who were slain.

l: captains of hundreds, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Five captains of hundreds were named: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri, and Jehoiada took them into covenant with him. Jehoiada gave them David's spears, bucklers, and shields, and later directed them to bring Athaliah out between the ranks. They also helped bring the king down to his house and set him on the throne.

l: people of Judah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: The people of Judah, with the heads of fathers' households, came to Jerusalem and made a covenant with the king in God's house. They stood in the courts with weapons around the king, rejoiced and blew trumpets at his crowning, and broke down the house of Baal, its altars and images, and killed Mattan its priest. They rejoiced after Athaliah's death, and the city was quiet.

l: covenant, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: has_purpose make the people the LORD's people [between Jehoiada, all the people, and the king] A covenant appears at several stages: Jehoiada's covenant with the captains of hundreds, the assembly's covenant with the king in God's house, and the covenant given to the king at his crowning. Jehoiada then made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king that they should be the LORD's people.

l: coronation of the king, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: The king's son was brought out, crowned, given the covenant, made king, and anointed by Jehoiada and his sons, with the people saying 'Long live the king!' The people rejoiced, trumpeters stood by the king, and singers led praise with instruments. Later he was set on the throne of the kingdom.

l: killing of Athaliah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: After Athaliah cried 'Treason!', Jehoiada ordered her brought out between the ranks, with anyone following her to be slain, and insisted she not be killed in the LORD's house. She was made way for, went to the entrance of the horse gate to the king's house, and was killed there. Afterward the people rejoiced and the city was quiet.

l: Amaziah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Amaziah, son of Joash and Jehoaddan, became king of Judah at twenty-five and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, doing right but without a perfect heart. After defeating Seir he worshiped its gods, ignored a prophet, challenged Israel and lost, then fled a conspiracy to Lachish, was killed, and was buried with his fathers.

l: priests and Levites, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: was_tasked_by Joash [to gather money for repairs; did not act right away] Joash gathered the priests and Levites and told them to collect money from the cities of Judah to repair the house, but the Levites did not act right away. Later Levites carried the chest to the king's officers when it was full.

l: princes of Judah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: The princes of Judah first rejoiced and gave to the chest, but after Jehoiada's death they swayed Joash, leading to abandonment of the LORD's house for Asherah poles and idols, and the Syrians later destroyed them.

l: chest, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: A chest made at the king's command and placed outside the gate of the LORD's house to collect Moses' tax. Princes and people filled it; the scribe and chief priest's officer emptied it daily, gathering abundant money.

l: temple repair, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Joash intended to restore the LORD's house; after the Levites' delay, tax money collected in a chest funded it, and Jehoiada with the king paid workers. Masons, carpenters and metalworkers rebuilt and strengthened it, and leftover money became ministering vessels.

l: killing of Zechariah, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada, is stoned in the LORD's house court by conspirators on King Joash's order, forgetting Jehoiada's kindness. Zechariah asks the LORD to repay it; Syrian defeat follows, then Joash's servants murder him for Jehoiada's sons' blood.

l: Seir, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: has_gods gods of Seir The children of Seir were struck down, ten thousand of them, by Amaziah in the Valley of Salt. Ten thousand more were taken alive by Judah and thrown from the top of a rock, so that all were broken in pieces. Amaziah afterward took their gods home.

l: gods of Seir, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Amaziah brought the gods of the children of Seir home, set them up as his own, bowed to them, and burned incense to them. A prophet asked why he sought gods that had not delivered their own people from his hand. This idolatry provoked the LORD's anger.

l: Joash king of Israel, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: Joash, king of Israel and son of Jehoahaz, answered Amaziah's challenge with a thistle-and-cedar parable, then defeated Judah at Beth Shemesh, captured Amaziah, breached Jerusalem's wall, and took treasures and hostages to Samaria.

l: Beth Shemesh, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: belongs_to Judah Beth Shemesh, a place belonging to Judah, is where Joash and Amaziah met face to face. Judah was defeated there, and Joash took Amaziah captive at that place.

l: battle of Beth Shemesh, The Second Book of Chronicles
s: At Beth Shemesh, Amaziah's challenge drew Joash of Israel to battle; Judah was defeated and every man fled to his tent, which the text attributes to God for seeking Edom's gods.
